prompt:
Create ONE new finished Sdorica-style character illustration, vertical 2:3. Use the FIRST reference as the governing art direction: its carefully designed broad curved shapes, restrained painterly color planes, smooth continuous contours, calm controlled values and understated material shading. Match that deliberate 2D illustration language, not a realistic splash painting. Ignore its title, miniature character, shield, black background and speckled outer vignette. The SECOND reference supplies ONLY the redheaded adult woman's facial likeness and delicate drawn facial features; do not use its hairstyle detail, costume or pose.

Subject: an adult female archer with red high ponytail, amber eyes, a compact gold hair clasp, deep violet tailored combat clothing, warm antique-gold armor accents, and an ivory recurved bow. Her face has the second reference's gentle hand-drawn eyes, natural cheek and chin construction, subtle nose and mouth and warm matte skin, now looking intently along her arrow.

Pose: a low sliding stop at full draw, close low three-quarter viewpoint. Torso upright over a low pelvis, one leg extended diagonally toward the lower-right foreground, the other bent deeply toward image left with its foot folded beneath her. Keep the entire ribcage-waist-pelvis connection and leg joints believable. Her bow arm reaches to image right, drawing hand anchors beside her jaw; the arrow nock meets the two taut string segments there, one straight arrow rests immediately above the bow grip. Natural hands. This is an energetic low grounded pose, not standing or jumping.

REDESIGN THE SHAPES FROM THE FIRST REFERENCE:
Hair is ONE large flowing ponytail mass, branching into just FOUR substantial overlapping curved locks. All locks visibly emerge from the same tie, share one swept direction, and end in clean tapered tips. Draw at most two small loose face-framing wisps. Shade the whole hair volume with ONE connected light family and ONE connected shadow family from an upper-left light source; broad red-orange light planes, deep burgundy underside. No individual hair-strand highlights, wiry flyaways, splinters or tangled separated strands.
Armor uses intact gently curved plates, rounded shoulder caps, simple fitted forearm guards and articulated knee/shin plates with a narrow ankle transition. Each major plate has one elegant inset curved ornament and an understated rim, like the first reference. NO serrations, jagged layered shards, spikes, blade fins, little golden triangles or mirror reflections. Richness comes from designed curves, thickness and coordinated ornament.
Clothing has continuous large violet surfaces, a functional waist belt with ONE beautiful clasp, and exactly TWO broad short overskirt panels visibly sewn at the hips, with a restrained cream lining. Their smooth hems end near the knees and their folds start from the waist and bent hips. NO separate ribbons, tassels, floating tails, shredded hems or extra drapery. Keep a complete appealing costume, not a plain uniform.

Finish: clean deliberate curved edges, economical internal lines, subtle tonal transitions contained inside large shapes. Restrained satin-metal shading, broad cloth shadows, matte skin, specific expressive face. No chipped paint, dry-brush tears, noisy paper overlay, grunge, hatching, stipple or fragmented highlights. Preserve sophistication through proportion, edge control, palette and ornament placement.
Background: quiet warm ivory with one broad pale blue-gray architectural silhouette in the distance and one uninterrupted pale cloud wash. Feet contact a single simple stone plane with clear contact shadow; no pebbles, random cracks, splashes, rubble fields or texture noise. The character dominates. Keep head, hands and leg structure clearly readable. No text, logo, frame, grid or additional characters.
